category: shared model inference API and dedicated GPU instances

free_tier.stated: evroc's own documentation states Shared Models have 'no minimum spend' and bill 'per million tokens (input and output separately)'; some models also support cached input tokens at a reduced rate. The API is at https://models.think.evroc.com/v1 with 16 models listed by models.dev. No always-free token allowance is published on evroc's own pages. A separate GPU-VM campaign page advertises 'Get €500 free credits', with no terms for the Think API on that page.
free_tier.notes: The 500-euro credit is on the GPU VM campaign page, not on the Think Models pricing documentation, and its eligibility is not stated there. Per-token figures for specific models are published by models.dev, a third-party catalogue; evroc's own pricing documentation states the billing shape but no per-model rate table was found on evroc's own pages.

per_object_cap.stated: Not an object store: the unit is tokens through an OpenAI-compatible inference API. models.dev lists context windows from 448 tokens for Whisper models to 524,288 for GLM-5.2, and output limits from 448 to 262,144 tokens.
per_object_cap.notes: Dedicated Model Instances use instance sizes such as 1-b200-27c-240g; GPU VMs offer 1 to 8 GPUs per instance.

retention.stated: The shared inference API holds no user objects: a request is billed by tokens and no storage or retention period is stated. Dedicated Model Instances run continuously until the user deletes them.
retention.notes: No retention clause was read on the Think documentation pages.

egress.terms: No egress charge or allowance is stated on evroc's Think documentation or its cloud-services pages. The object-storage calculator on evroc's own site prices 1 GB of storage at EUR 0.02 per month and 0 GB downloaded monthly at EUR 0.00 outbound, but no Think API egress term is published.

interface_detail: OpenAI-compatible REST API at https://models.think.evroc.com/v1 with standard clients and LangChain; the evroc CLI manages model instances and API keys.
tooling: Standard OpenAI-compatible clients, LangChain and the evroc CLI; the models.dev package is @ai-sdk/openai-compatible.
chaining: A shared model endpoint can be swapped in for another OpenAI-compatible backend with a configuration change, while dedicated GPU instances give predictable hourly cost for a pinned model.

limits.value: rate limits apply to Shared Models; HTTP 429 when too many requests and 503 under high load, with Retry-After; the exact thresholds are subject to change
the API is team-scoped and a key is required: an unauthenticated GET to https://models.think.evroc.com/v1/models answered 401 with 106 bytes on 2026-11-24

limits_note: evroc states the service is busiest 09-17h European time and recommends non-interactive work outside those hours. The exact request thresholds are not published.
binding_note: The shared endpoint's rate limit binds first because its thresholds are undisclosed and can change, and the service returns 429 or 503 under load; the per-token charge is a price, not a capacity ceiling.

identity_cost.detail: evroc's sign-up page at https://signup.evroc.com/ renders only 'Get started with evroc', a log-in link and a link to speak to a Cloud Specialist; no fields were visible in the captured page. The user documentation says 'You create an API key, pick a model from the supported models list', so an account and a key are required before a request. Which registration fields the signup form asks for is unverified: behind an incomplete signup form.

reliability_note: Shared Models are busiest 09-17h European time; the service answers 429 when rate limited and 503 with no server available under high load, with a Retry-After header. The exact thresholds are not published and may change.
confidence_note: The billing shape, no-minimum-spend statement, API endpoint, rate-limit statuses and busy hours are quoted from evroc's own documentation read 2026-11-24; the 500-euro credit is quoted from evroc's GPU VM campaign page. The 401 on the models endpoint is from a probe registered with --probe. Signup fields could not be read, and no per-model rate table was found on evroc's own pages, so those are left unverified.

notes: Hosted inference service: evroc operates the GPUs and the user calls an API, so nothing is installed or maintained by the user. The Think Shared Models tier has no always-free token allowance on evroc's own pages; the 500-euro credit is a GPU VM campaign offer with unstated eligibility. A separate Dedicated Model Instances tier bills per GPU-hour and is not priced here. The signup form fields could not be read and are unverified.

extras.billing_model: per-million-token for Shared Models; per GPU-hour for Dedicated Model Instances
extras.price_note: evroc's own Think documentation states the shape (input/output per million tokens, cached input at a reduced rate) but no first-party per-model rate table was captured; models.dev reports third-party per-model rates such as $0.114 / $0.114 for multilingual E5.
